report.headline: The STRENGTH trial of omega-3 carboxylic acids (Epanova) was stopped early for futility in January 2020 after an independent data monitoring committee concluded the drug was unlikely to show cardiovascular benefit.
report.summary: STRENGTH randomized approximately 13,086 statin-treated patients with triglycerides 175–499 mg/dL to Epanova 4 g/day or corn oil placebo, targeting a broad MACE composite including coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina. The trial planned 1,600 events over a median 3-year follow-up but was halted before reaching that threshold. The calculator could not predict an outcome because no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change was measured in the phase 3 population — only within-arm phase 2 reductions of –26% to –31% — leaving the expected effect size unknown. The primary reason for failure is classified as insufficient data, with design choices (corn oil placebo, soft endpoints) and uncertainty about whether triglyceride lowering per se is causal as contributing factors. Confidence in this assessment is medium.
key_evidence: ~13,086 patients randomized (Assessment of omega-3 carboxylic acids in statin-treated patients with high levels of triglycerides and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol: Rationale and design of the STRENGTH trial; Update on Phase III STRENGTH trial for Epanova in mixed dyslipidaemia)
Inclusion required triglycerides 175–499 mg/dL (Update on Phase III STRENGTH trial for Epanova in mixed dyslipidaemia)

Primary endpoint: time to first CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina (Assessment of omega-3 carboxylic acids in statin-treated patients with high levels of triglycerides and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol: Rationale and design of the STRENGTH trial)

Planned 1,600 primary endpoint events (Assessment of omega-3 carboxylic acids in statin-treated patients with high levels of triglycerides and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol: Rationale and design of the STRENGTH trial)

Median follow-up 3 years (Assessment of omega-3 carboxylic acids in statin-treated patients with high levels of triglycerides and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol: Rationale and design of the STRENGTH trial)

No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured; only within-arm phase 2 reductions of –26% (Effects of free omega-3 carboxylic acids and fenofibrate on liver fat content in patients with hypertriglyceridemia and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease) and –31% (Assessment of omega-3 carboxylic acids in statin-treated patients with high levels of triglycerides and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol: Rationale and design of the STRENGTH trial)
Trial stopped early for futility per IDMC recommendation (Update on Phase III STRENGTH trial for Epanova in mixed dyslipidaemia)
Calculator MDE HR 0.869 at 80% power; category insufficient_data, weakest link: triglycerides change not measured (calculator)
report.what_would_change_this: A placebo-adjusted triglyceride or apoB change from a phase 3 trial of Epanova 4 g/day in the STRENGTH population would allow the calculator to estimate expected benefit. Final STRENGTH results with hazard ratio and confidence interval would clarify whether the corn oil placebo or endpoint composition contributed to the null result.
report.readthrough_note: REDUCE-IT used pure EPA (icosapent ethyl) and showed benefit in a similar population, but STRENGTH tested EPA+DHA carboxylic acids with a corn oil placebo; the different formulation and placebo choice limit direct read-through to other omega-3 programmes.

mechanism.notes: No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change available for Epanova 4g/day in STRENGTH population. Only phase 2 within-arm data exists (-26% at 12 weeks, f_055846c61d587f). Baseline TG taken as inclusion threshold lower bound (175 mg/dL, f_e3ff0b15fb7650). Trial stopped early for futility before reaching 1600 planned events; actual event count at stoppage not reported. No phase 3 biomarker data. HDL-C and IL-6 changes from mouse studies (f_7684ecccf74fd1, f_2b5a8d3503ec1a) not included as not human, not same dose, not placebo-adjusted.

for.text: No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured in the outcome trial population or in a phase 3 trial of the same dose/formulation. The only TG data are within-arm phase 2 values (-26% at 4g, 12 weeks, pmid:30197273; -31% at 4g daily, pmid:30125052), which the calculator flags as 'not placebo-adjusted' and cannot use.
Calculator returns 'not_computable' with weakest_link 'triglycerides change not measured' and category 'insufficient_data'.

hypotheses.would_settle: A placebo-adjusted triglyceride change from a phase 3 trial of Epanova 4g/day in the STRENGTH population (or the STRENGTH trial itself if biomarker substudy exists).

for.text: Reference table lists 'triglycerides: causal=uncertain' and 'triglycerides (via apoB): causal=yes', indicating uncertainty whether TG lowering per se is causal or only via apoB-containing particles.
STRENGTH used omega-3-carboxylic acids (EPA+DHA) while REDUCE-IT used pure EPA (icosapent ethyl); different formulations may have different effects on apoB and other atherogenic particles.

against.text: Mendelian randomization studies support causal role of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (via apoB) in CVD; if Epanova lowers apoB, benefit would be expected.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted change in apoB or non-HDL-C from a phase 3 trial of Epanova 4g/day; genetic evidence specific to the drug's molecular targets.

for.text: Corn oil placebo may have adverse effects: in REDUCE-IT, mineral oil placebo increased LDL-C and possibly events; corn oil (used in STRENGTH) may similarly increase LDL-C or inflammation, diluting the treatment difference.
Primary endpoint is a broad MACE composite including coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina — softer endpoints less likely to be prevented by lipid-lowering.
Trial stopped early for futility (2020-01-13) before reaching planned 1600 events, reducing power and potentially missing a late-emerging benefit.

against.text: REDUCE-IT used a similar broad MACE endpoint and showed a clear benefit with icosapent ethyl.

hypotheses.would_settle: Final STRENGTH results with HR and CI; comparison of placebo-group LDL-C trajectory in STRENGTH vs REDUCE-IT.

for.text: Inclusion required TG 175-499 mg/dL (moderate hypertriglyceridemia) on statins; residual risk in this population may be driven more by non-lipid factors (inflammation, thrombosis) than by TG-rich lipoproteins.

against.text: REDUCE-IT enrolled a similar population (TG 135-499 mg/dL on statins) and showed benefit.

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analysis of STRENGTH by baseline TG, apoB, or inflammatory markers; comparison of baseline characteristics with REDUCE-IT.

for.text: If the true placebo-adjusted TG reduction is substantially smaller than the within-arm -26% (e.g., due to placebo group changes or regression to mean), the expected RRR could be below the trial's MDE (HR 0.869 at 80% power).

against.text: Without placebo-adjusted data, the expected effect size is unknown — not zero, but unquantifiable.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted TG and apoB changes from a phase 3 trial of Epanova 4g/day.

for.text: Calculator input lists target_genetics as 'uncertain' (no genetic evidence found for omega-3-carboxylic acids targets).

against.text: 'Uncertain' reflects absence of evidence, not evidence of no effect; omega-3 fatty acids act on multiple pathways (TG synthesis, inflammation, membrane effects) not captured by a single genetic target.

hypotheses.would_settle: Human genetic studies of the specific molecular targets engaged by omega-3-carboxylic acids (e.g., GPR120, PPAR pathways).

for.text: No safety signal reported in the futility announcement; the statement only addresses lack of benefit.

against.text: Omega-3 carboxylic acids generally well tolerated; no known off-target harm that would offset cardiovascular benefit.

hypotheses.would_settle: Full safety data from STRENGTH final report.

for.text: Trial stopped early by independent data monitoring committee for futility — a scientific, not business, decision.

against.text: Enrollment completed (13,078-13,086 randomized); median follow-up 3 years achieved; no evidence of poor adherence or recruitment issues.

hypotheses.would_settle: Final publication with adherence and discontinuation rates.

issues.issue: Calculator input includes a non-placebo-adjusted triglyceride change (-26% from phase 2 EFFECT I, f_055846c61d587f) as if it were a valid biomarker input. The accepted input for autopsy mode is a placebo-adjusted phase 2 change at the outcome trial dose; since no such value exists, the 'changes' array should be empty (or contain only null entries) with a 'missing' note explaining the absence of placebo-adjusted data. The current input passes a within-arm value that the calculator correctly rejects, but the case should not present it as a quantified input.
issues.request: Remove the non-placebo-adjusted TG change from calculator inputs.changes (set to empty array) and add a 'missing' field noting 'No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change available for Epanova 4g/day in STRENGTH population; phase 2 data (EFFECT I, pmid:30197273) are within-arm only.'

issues.issue: Hypotheses list 'biomarker_not_causal' as a secondary category (status: undetermined) when the calculator's primary category is 'insufficient_data' with weakest_link 'triglycerides change not measured'. Without a quantified placebo-adjusted biomarker effect, any causal assessment of triglycerides is speculative. The secondary categories should only include hypotheses that can be evaluated given the available data (e.g., 'design_or_endpoint' is supported; 'biomarker_not_causal' and 'effect_too_small' should be noted as unevaluable due to missing data, not listed as secondary categories).
issues.request: Restrict secondary_categories to only those with evaluable evidence given missing biomarker data (i.e., keep 'design_or_endpoint'; move 'biomarker_not_causal' and 'effect_too_small' to a 'cannot_evaluate_due_to_missing_biomarker_data' note). Update hypotheses accordingly.

issues.issue: Multiple inclusion threshold values for triglycerides appear in verified facts (180 mg/dL from pmid:30125052, 100 mg/dL for LDL-C from same, 175-499 mg/dL from announcement). The calculator input uses baseline 175 mg/dL (matching announcement lower bound) but the case does not clarify which threshold reflects the final protocol. The announcement (2020-01-13) is the most recent source and likely reflects the final protocol.
issues.request: Add a note in the case clarifying that the final protocol (per announcement) used TG 175-499 mg/dL, and that earlier publications cited varying thresholds.

issues.issue: n_randomized values differ slightly across sources: 13,078 (CTgov), 13,086 (pmid:30125052 and announcement). The calculator does not use n_randomized, but the case should note the discrepancy and use the most recent authoritative source (announcement: 13,086).
issues.request: Add a note documenting the n_randomized discrepancy and stating that 13,086 (from announcement) is used as the final randomized count.
